_comment: Source of truth for the projects grid on the homepage.
Edit this file, then run: python3 scripts/build_projects.py
slug    — internal id, must be unique
blurb   — one or two sentences: what it is and who it is for
learned — what building it taught you. Admissions committees read this
line more carefully than the tech tags. Be specific.
tags    — technologies you would be happy to be questioned on
links   — live, source, doc are all optional; omit or null to hide.
doc is a third link (a write-up or deck); docLabel names it.
repo    — 'owner/name' for a PUBLIC GitHub repo, or null.
Stats are fetched only when this is set and the repo is public.
stats   — filled in automatically. Do not edit by hand.

projects.title: Setu
projects.blurb: A working prototype of a public procurement route where a government department posts a problem, an independent evaluator picks a startup, and a paid pilot converts into a contract. Built for the Smart India Hackathon problem statement on startup-friendly procurement.
projects.learned: Separating the roles was the decision worth defending: the department that writes the problem does not choose the winner, an evaluator does, and every rejection carries a written reason the applicant can read. The constraint that shaped the build was this site's content security policy — no inline styles or scripts are allowed, so the whole thing is external CSS and JS with the one genuinely dynamic value set through the CSSOM instead.

projects.title: Survibe
projects.blurb: A piano learning app for iPad that listens as you play and teaches in real time — no cables, no theory homework.
projects.learned: Shipping end to end: real-time audio, a design system, a strict content security policy, and a live domain on Cloudflare. The hard part was never the code, it was deciding what to leave out.
